task.title: L9: adaptive time budgets, job-status contract, honest progress and ETA
task.objective: Finish Phase L L9 (awkit-djnl.13) as docs/plans/ai-upgrade-v5/L9-adaptive-time-progress-eta.md defines it. L9.1: one job-status contract (state, queue position and hold reason, stage, elapsed, ETA range with confidence and cold or warm, effective profile, cancel, terminal reason) emitted by AiService and the model and backend-pack jobs, pushed to the owning window only. L9.2: a bounded per-feature budget table (locator assistance, authoring explanation, failure analysis, fragment assistance, model load, compatibility probe, component copy) whose defaults are the historical evidence values, configurable only within committed bounds and refused outside them, kept apart from benchmark ceilings, cancel grace and ETA ranges; a changed budget never re-labels old quality evidence. L9.3: one shared accessible progress component, determinate only with a known denominator (copy bytes, the runtime's own load progress), generation indeterminate, never a percentage from elapsed time, throttled polite announcements, reduced motion. L9.4: bounded, versioned, non-sensitive ETA aggregates keyed by the latency class (quality key plus hardware class) under LOCALAPPDATA, written atomically. L9.5: every AI feature surface and Settings wired, with packaged live-model evidence on the development machine in each L8a mode.

security: No new permission: job status is readable only by the window that owns the job (AI_USE), model-job cancellation is AI_MANAGE, budgets change only through ai:updateSettings (AI_MANAGE with re-authentication).
Job status, ETA history and budgets carry codes, stage names, numbers and quality-key identifiers only; never a prompt, page text, response, path, device name or credential.
The host's progress messages carry a stage and a fraction only, for the request that asked; the main process validates them and drops anything malformed.
offline: Nothing is downloaded. The ETA history lives under the runtime data root, never in resources. The host change regenerates the signed dependency manifest through a fresh package from a clean tree.
AI stays optional: no inference is added to the run path, and every job surface degrades to a code when AI is off or unavailable.

acceptance.description: Fake-clock deterministic proof of every state and stage transition, queue position and hold, timeout and cancel recovery, determinate and indeterminate semantics, cold and warm profile-aware ETA ranges, no-history behavior, bounded budgets refused out of range, settings migration and the persisted, capped, versioned, non-sensitive ETA history; every new verifier mutation-tested once green.
The host reports the runtime's own load progress and the first generated token for the request that asked, nothing else; every new guard mutation-tested.

Real Electron: determinate and indeterminate bars, reduced motion, keyboard, screen-reader names and the focus contract on every affected surface, budgets in Settings refused out of range, ETA persisted across restart.
The new channels are gated and rostered, the run path still reaches no model, qualification reads a changed budget as unqualified.
On a fresh package on the development machine, a real model's jobs report real load progress, stages, no-history, cold and warm ETA persisted across a restart, in each L8a mode.
Typecheck, bundles, script typecheck and the verifier registry pass.
